always_background.zero_overlap_convention: GT-positive frames with TP=0 / all GT-positive frames; includes empty and spatially disjoint predictions, unlike the no-foreground missed_positive_frame_rate

group_bootstrap.method: percentile; resample explicit groups with replacement, retain all member frames
group_bootstrap.caveat: group_id must identify independent parent/site units; independence is not inferred or verified

always_background.additional_metric_convention: Micro ratios use pooled pixel counts; undefined denominators are null. Positive-only Dice includes GT-positive frames only. False alarms are any predicted foreground on GT-negative frames / GT-negative frames; missed positive frames have no predicted foreground / GT-positive frames (not spatial misses).
always_background.role: Held-out CROSS-SOURCE distress test. Different sensor, resolution (512x512 vs Crack-Seg 416x416) and geography from the training source. Not an Indian test and not a substitute for live capture.
always_background.negative_caveat: CRKWH100 is a crack dataset: every one of the 100 images carries crack ground truth, so this set supplies NO negatives. False-alarm behaviour still cannot be measured from available data.

limitations: No predictions from a trained model, no fitting, and no threshold selection.
Baseline results establish a comparison floor on the supplied labels, not useful road detection.
All-foreground pixel recall of 1 is trivial and is not a model achievement.
Always-background precision can be 1 under legacy empty-denominator conventions despite missed defects; read recall, positive-only Dice and pooled counts.
Missing independent group metadata suppresses group intervals; dataset names or filename order do not prove independence.
No verified physical units or Indian/live acceptance claim is made.
